sections.html:
You will find the office on the courthouse's third floor, 119 Justice Drive, Suite 9, Winton. Call 252-358-7850. Doors are open weekdays from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, minus county holidays and closings.

Staff keep real estate documents going back as far as 1862, and land deeds in the area date to 1710. Its shelves include deeds, deeds of trust, maps, military discharge and notary records, and vital records for local births, deaths and marriages. The index is by name, so a lawyer tracing an old farm tract works backward through owners.

Fees can change, as the posted schedule itself cautions, so phone ahead before mailing a check. Mailed returns need a self-addressed stamped envelope.

Real estate fees, Hertford County Register of Deeds

Plat copies run $3.00 a page. Fax or online copy requests are $1.00 for the first page and $.25 for every later one.

sections.h2: Formatting rules and the nonstandard fee
sections.html:
Paper standards come from G.S. 161-14. Miss them and the office records the document anyway, adding the $25.00 fee.

  • Letter or legal size paper, one side only
  • Black type on white, 10 point or larger
  • Wide blank band across the head of page one

A drafter rule comes from Session Law 2011-351: whoever prepared a deed or deed of trust, person or law firm, is named on page one. Each deed also needs the tax parcel pin. For delinquent taxes the office wants one of two things, a tax department stamp showing none or wording that sends the closing attorney to pay back taxes out of proceeds. E-filed deeds must use the wording.

Yes, for everything but maps. Corporation Service Company and Simplifile are the named submitters, and the recorded copy returns electronically right after recording.

Your closing attorney picks the route, so a seller normally has nothing to submit personally.

Paper filers should enclose a check made out to the Register of Deeds with a working phone number written on it. Maps, which cannot be e-recorded, have to go in on paper.

sections.h2: What the office cannot do for a seller
sections.html:
Sellers often call the register for help it cannot give. Knowing the limits saves a trip.

  • It cannot search a title, because state law bars register staff from doing so. An individual or a legal representative can run the search.
  • It cannot confirm whether a lien exists. A recorded deed of trust is your clue that the property secured a loan.
  • It cannot alter a recorded deed. Fixing one takes a new deed, and the office suggests an attorney.
  • An owner cannot be named from a street address, because the index runs by name. Land Records Mapping, at 252-358-7809, handles location questions.
  • It holds no estate, will or divorce records. Those sit with the Clerk of Superior Court, 252-358-7100.

Real estate documents are online, though older indexes and images may not be.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax?
sections.html:
Sellers carry it. G.S. 105-228.30 assigns the burden to the transferor, at the $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price shown on the fee schedule.

A conveyance binds later purchasers and lien creditors only after registration under G.S. 47-18, so record soon after signing. Read both rules at G.S. 105-228.30 and G.S. 47-18.

sections.h2: Other services at the Winton counter
sections.html:
Vital records and a few other items come through this counter, which helps if you also need paperwork for an estate or a move.

  • Certified birth, death or marriage copy: $10.00 each with government photo ID, released only to close relatives or an authorized agent.
  • Online vital record requests: $3.50 added, through the county's Get Certificate Now program.
  • Notary oath: $10.00, no appointment needed once the Secretary of State sends notice.
  • Military discharge filing and certified copy: free, though discharges are not open to public viewing.

Population is about 19,015 as of mid 2025, spread over 9,873 housing units. A median owned home is $119,200, and 67.4 percent of homes are lived in by owners. With values this modest, flat charges like recording fees take a bigger bite out of a small sale, so get the closing attorney's cost list before pricing.

sections.h2: The 2027 revaluation and deeds recorded now
sections.html:
The county's revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, the first since 2019, and field measuring began in July 2025. Recording steps stay the same for deeds filed before or after that date. Only the assessed value on the parcel changes.

The Tax Assessor and Tax Collector sit at 115 Justice Drive in Winton. Ask the collector about the current bill before you close. The county also warns the public about deed scams, with a fraud detection page linked from the Register of Deeds site.

sections.h2: A seller's path through the office
sections.html:
Before closing, ask your attorney to confirm the deed will name you exactly as the record owner. A mistake means a new deed, since the office cannot change one already recorded. Check that page one names the preparer and carries the tax parcel pin, and that the deed includes the sentence directing back taxes to be paid from closing proceeds. Ask the Tax Collector for a payoff so no delinquent tax holds up the deed.

On closing day the seller's excise tax of $2.00 per $1000.00 is collected with the recording. Any paid-off deed of trust is cancelled at no fee. Recording is what protects the buyer against later purchasers and lien creditors, so ask the attorney to send the deed promptly. An e-recorded copy comes back electronically. A cash sale skips the lender's deed of trust, which means one fewer instrument to record and one less satisfaction to chase.

If something goes wrong after closing, such as a misspelled name or a missing page, call the office at 252-358-7850 right away. Staff can tell you what was recorded, but the fix is a new deed prepared by an attorney. For questions about where a parcel sits, Land Records Mapping at 252-358-7809 is the right call, and for estate or divorce papers tied to the sale, the Clerk of Superior Court at 252-358-7100 holds them.

faqs.q: How much does Hertford County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The schedule lists $26.00 for a general instrument up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per extra page, and $64.00 for a deed of trust up to 35 pages. Call 252-358-7850 to check for changes.

faqs.q: What is the excise tax on a deed?
faqs.a: The county lists $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price, and the seller pays it.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed is formatted wrong?
faqs.a: It is recorded anyway, with a $25.00 non-standard fee added. Check the paper, type and page one rules above before you file.

faqs.q: Can staff search my title or find a lien?
faqs.a: No. State law keeps register staff from searching titles, and the office cannot confirm whether a lien exists. An attorney or title professional can read the recorded instruments.

faqs.q: Can I get a copy of my recorded deed?
faqs.a: Yes, at the counter or on the county sites, though older indexes and images may be missing online. Certified copies are priced per page.
